diagnosis: Urinary schistosomiasis with a calcified bladder
symptom: a little blood at the end of every pee for months
hook: the bladder looked like a thin eggshell drawn in white chalk
whatYouSee: A thin white rim of calcium outlines the whole bladder wall like an eggshell sitting just above the pubic bone.
whyItMatters: Schistosoma haematobium eggs lodge in the bladder wall and calcify. The worm is caught by wading or swimming in fresh water that carries infected snails. Chronic infection raises the risk of squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder.
treatment: Praziquantel kills the adult worms. Long-standing disease needs follow-up for ureteric obstruction and bladder cancer.
takeaway: Eggshell calcification of the bladder wall in someone from an endemic area is schistosomiasis until proven otherwise.

condition.keyFindings: Plain AP radiograph of the lower abdomen and pelvis (KUB view) with the bottom edge of the film at the top of the pubic symphysis. A thin smooth continuous curvilinear rim of calcification outlines the whole wall of the urinary bladder in the midline of the pelvis, forming a round to oval white ring like an eggshell or the outline of a fetal head sitting just above the pubic bone. The inside of the bladder is uniform soft tissue grey. Fine thin linear calcification also runs along the distal ureters on both sides as they enter the bladder. The sacrum, iliac bones, hip joints, lower lumbar spine and bowel gas pattern look normal.

defects: Unexplained additional image findings: ["Blurred gray rectangular mask over the lower pelvis/perineum, a non-anatomic overlay that obscures the pubic symphysis and the region the expected view should show","Prominent rounded gas-filled loops projecting over the right iliac wing and left iliac wing region, which are probably bowel but look somewhat disconnected from the colonic frame","Both kidney outlines appear as vague rounded densities with no clear discrete renal margins"]

findings: Frontal AP supine abdominopelvic radiograph covering the lower thoracic/upper abdomen to the proximal femora and pelvis, with a blurred or obscured region over the lower pelvis/perineum, likely deliberate masking.
Thin linear calcification with a tram-track or beaded appearance follows the expected course of both ureters from the level of the kidneys down to the bladder.
A rounded pelvic soft-tissue density, consistent with a bladder, has a thin curvilinear calcified rim along its upper and lateral walls.
Both ureteral and bladder wall calcifications are bilateral and fairly symmetric.
Renal outlines are poorly defined, with faint rounded soft-tissue densities in both flanks. No definite discrete calculus is seen.
Gas-filled loops of colon are distributed around the periphery without marked dilatation. A gas-filled stomach bubble is present in the left upper quadrant.
The lumbar spine appears to have degenerative or osteopenic change with a coarse trabecular pattern. The sacroiliac joints and hips appear grossly congruent, with no displaced fracture identified.
Image has notable grain/noise and a dark left margin.
differential: Chronic bilateral urinary tract calcification (ureteral and bladder wall), most consistent with chronic granulomatous infection such as genitourinary tuberculosis or schistosomiasis
Chronic cystitis/ureteritis with dystrophic wall calcification from other causes (e.g., prior radiation, chemotherapy, or chronic infection)
Phleboliths or vascular calcification mimicking ureteral/bladder wall calcification (less likely given the continuous linear tubular course)
anatomyConcerns: The lower pelvic blur obscures the perineal and pubic region and appears to be an overlay, not anatomy.
No impossible anatomy is identified. The tubular calcifications follow plausible ureteral and bladder anatomy.
The poor image quality limits assessment of the renal outlines and subtle calculi.
